prompt: Points $A$ and $B$ are the ends of a diameter of a circle, and $C$ is another point on the circle. What is the measure of $\angle ACB$?
hint: $\angle ACB$ is an inscribed angle — its vertex $C$ sits on the circle and it intercepts the arc from $A$ to $B$.

hints.text: $\angle ACB$ is an inscribed angle — its vertex $C$ sits on the circle and it intercepts the arc from $A$ to $B$.
Since $\overline{AB}$ is a diameter, the intercepted arc is a semicircle: $180^\circ$.
Half of $180^\circ$ is $90^\circ$ — a right angle, no matter where $C$ sits.

explanation: A diameter splits the circle into two $180^\circ$ arcs.
$\angle ACB$ is inscribed and intercepts one of those semicircular arcs.
Inscribed angle $=$ half the arc $= \frac{180}{2} = 90^\circ$. Choice C.

alternativeExplanations.title: Slide C around and watch
steps: Move $C$ anywhere on the upper half of the circle — near $A$, near $B$, or right on top.
The triangle changes shape completely, but the angle at $C$ stays a perfect right angle every time. That is Thales' theorem.
